section_title: Private banking and wealth management risks > Money laundering risks associated with private banking and wealth management

cards.title: Screen inherent private banking financial crime risk drivers
cards.summary: Screen private banking and wealth management activity against inherent risk drivers created by profitability, discretion, relationship incentives, and AUM-based compensation.
cards.scenario: Private banking and wealth management for high-net-worth and ultrahigh-net-worth customers.
cards.objective: Identify inherent financial crime risk drivers in the private banking model.

flow_nodes.label: Private banking or wealth management context exists
flow_nodes.source_quote: Private banking and wealth management offer high-net-worth and ultrahigh-net-worth individuals personalized and confidential banking services... Private banking often operates semi-autonomously from other parts of a bank.

flow_nodes.label: Screen the private banking model for inherent financial crime risk drivers
High profitability and a culture of discretion and trust may generate financial crime risk
flow_nodes.source_quote: Some of the financial crime risks associated with private banking stem from its perceived high profitability... and the culture of discretion and trust...

flow_nodes.label: Close customer relationships may cause relationship managers to overlook warning signs
flow_nodes.source_quote: The desire to establish and maintain close relationships with their customers might cause relationship managers to overlook warning signs.

flow_nodes.label: Competition and AUM-based compensation pressure managers to obtain customers and increase AUM
flow_nodes.source_quote: Competition for high-net-worth individuals increases the pressure on relationship managers to obtain new customers, to increase their AUM...

flow_nodes.label: AUM compensation creates conflict of interest and may obscure high-risk activity from an AFC perspective
flow_nodes.source_quote: Due to this compensation structure, private banking managers might not recognize certain aspects of their customer activities as high risk from an AFC perspective.

flow_nodes.label: Inherent private banking and wealth management financial crime risk finding
flow_nodes.source_quote: This conflict of interest is an inherent risk of private banking and wealth management.

cards.review_notes: Risk-factor material is modeled as a risk_indicator card, not a strict operating workflow. The listed drivers are parallel screening standards connected with USES edges; the only PRECEDES edge is a structural context-to-screening dependency.

cards.title: Identify high-risk private banking customer profiles
cards.summary: Review private banking customers for example risk indicators involving opaque ownership, unjustified multi-jurisdictional wealth, and PEP exposure.
cards.trigger: Other examples of financial crime risk in private banking include specified customer characteristics.
cards.objective: Identify customer profile indicators that elevate financial crime risk.

flow_nodes.label: Private banking financial crime risk examples are being reviewed
flow_nodes.source_quote: Other examples of financial crime risk in private banking include:

flow_nodes.label: Review customer profile for high-risk private banking indicators
Use of private investment companies or complex ownership structures reduces UBO transparency
flow_nodes.source_quote: Customers who use private investment companies or complex ownership structures to reduce the transparency of the ultimate beneficial owners.

flow_nodes.label: Personal and business wealth is maintained in numerous jurisdictions without justified business reasons to evade tax
flow_nodes.source_quote: Customers who choose to maintain personal and business wealth in numerous jurisdictions without justified business reasons to evade tax.

flow_nodes.label: Customer is a PEP or has close associates who are PEPs, increasing bribery and corruption risk
flow_nodes.source_quote: Customers who are considered PEPs or have close associates who are PEPs increase the bribery and corruption risk of the business.

flow_nodes.label: Customer profile presents elevated private banking financial crime risk

cards.review_notes: The source lists examples of risk indicators rather than a chronological process. The indicators are modeled as parallel standard nodes used by a review action, with no PRECEDES chain among the risk factors.

cards.title: Apply governance controls to private banking risk management
cards.summary: Apply compliance oversight and performance-evaluation controls so risk management remains embedded in the private banker's role.
cards.scenario: Private banking governance and performance management.
cards.objective: Provide oversight, challenge the business, and keep risk management central to private banking performance.

flow_nodes.label: Private banking risk management controls are required
Empower the compliance department and make its approach robust
flow_nodes.source_quote: The compliance department must be empowered and robust...

flow_nodes.label: Proper oversight and challenge are provided to the business
flow_nodes.source_quote: ...providing proper oversight and challenges to the business.

flow_nodes.label: Use a balanced scorecard for performance evaluation
flow_nodes.source_quote: Business leaders should use a balanced scorecard for performance evaluation.

flow_nodes.label: Managing risk remains a fundamental part of the private banker's role
flow_nodes.source_quote: This ensures that managing risk remains a fundamental part of the private banker's role.

cards.review_notes: The two controls are parallel governance requirements, not a stated sequence. PRECEDES edges from the start node are structural entry dependencies; PRODUCES edges are explicit control-effect relationships from the source units.
